item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Architectures for New Social and Tourism Scenarios in Alpine Territories - Ref. 001/26/IR-MI (Politecnico TORINO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-11 15:00
Institution: Politecnico TORINO, Torino
Field: Civil engineering and architecture / 08/CEAR-09 Progettazione architettonica

The research aims to investigate how contemporary forms of Alpine tourism can become a driver of territorial and architectural regeneration in mountain areas. By envisioning pathways for enhancing local resources and strengthening communities, the research focuses on the adaptive reuse of disused buildings and infrastructures in mountain contexts, with the aim of outlining new development scenarios and fostering processes of social, cultural and economic innovation.

item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-03 23:59
Institution: ROMA "Tor Vergata", Roma, Rm
Field: Civil engineering and architecture / 08/CEAR-06 Scienza delle costruzioni

The research will develop multiscale computational models to investigate mechanisms governing atherosclerosis progression. Building on patient-specific biomechanical models, it will examine residual stresses, vascular growth and remodeling, and interactions between mechanical stimuli, inflammation and plaque composition. Mechanistic model identification strategies will integrate clinical data, imaging and biomarkers to describe disease progression

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Quantification of the intensification of sub-hourly extreme precipitation events in the Veneto Region using convection-permitting climate models (Univ. PADOVA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-30 23:59
Institution: Univ. PADOVA, Venezia
Field: Civil engineering and architecture / 08/CEAR-01 Idraulica, idrologia, costruzioni idrauliche e marittime

Assessment of changes in sub-hourly precipitation extremes across the Veneto Region under climate change. ARPAV records will be complemented with rain-gauge observations from ANBI-associated land reclamation consortia. At least nine convection-permitting climate models (CPMs) will be analysed for the historical period 1996–2005 and the future horizons 2041–2050 and 2090–2099 under RCP8.5. Statistical relationships between hourly and sub-hourly extremes will be used to estimate changes in short-duration rainfall and to develop rainfall depth–duration–frequency curves for multiple return periods.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Public space in Inland Mountain Regions - Ref. 123/26/IR (Politecnico TORINO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-03 15:00
Institution: Politecnico TORINO, Torino
Field: Civil engineering and architecture / 08/CEAR-09 Progettazione architettonica

The “Public Space in Inland and Mountain Regions” project is structured as a participatory action research initiative, designed to investigate, support, and systematize emerging forms of active citizenship. Through a transdisciplinary approach, the study redefines latent needs and local practices, evaluating current institutional policies and the effectiveness of existing philanthropic models in generating temporary or permanent impacts on the transformation and use of public spaces in small towns in inland and mountainous regions. The goal is to collaboratively design and update a philanthropic framework together with selected representatives of the Fondazione Compagnia di San Paolo.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Use of mechanical metamaterials with bistable cells for dynamic response control and seismic improvement - Ref. 122/26/IR (Politecnico TORINO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-03 15:00
Institution: Politecnico TORINO, Torino
Field: Civil engineering and architecture / 08/CEAR-07 Tecnica delle costruzioni

The project concerns the development of mechanical metamaterials based on bistable cells and multi-cell systems, which exploit snap-through mechanisms and nonlinear responses to dissipate energy and control vibrations. The research aims to assess their use as passive devices for controlling the dynamic response of structures and mechanical systems subjected to excitations of different nature, ranging vibrations to seismic actions, with focus on the seismic improvement of civil structures.

Field: Civil engineering and architecture / 08/CEAR-03 Infrastrutture e sistemi di trasporto, estimo e valutazione

The research focuses on the development of algorithms for analysis and economic evaluation, with a view to devising context-based urban design scenarios. The proposed tools are expected to adhere to principles of adaptation and mitigation in relation to the dynamics of urban development and the evolution of the relevant knowledge systems: property market, natural capital, socio-cultural assets. The study will also explore the potential use of artificial intelligence for the automation of evaluation processes in dynamic urban contexts.
